issues.body: `_review_fix_standdown_labels` walks every nested `ast.If` independently and collects a matching inner guard without considering its ancestors. For example, wrapping the live `if "review:parked" in labels: raise SystemExit(...)` in `if False:` leaves the returned label set unchanged and all three new checks green, while the workflow runs models on machine-parked PRs. The same problem occurs with other unreachable enclosing branches. This directly contradicts the function's claim that it recognizes an executed guard and misses the required conditionally-inert mutation of this trust check.
issues.fix_hint: Make the pin establish reachability from the heredoc's top-level admission path, not merely syntactic presence anywhere in the AST. Add a known-positive mutation that wraps the guard in a non-crashing false condition (and assert that the pristine and mutant sources differ) so this exact fail-open change produces a normal FAIL row.
issues.title: AST pin accepts a stand-down guard nested under dead control flow

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The literal-repoint and deletion checks improve coverage of the YAML seam, and the reconciliation test now observes the two machine-label writes using independent literal expectations. However, the new seam checker does not prove that the discovered guard is reachable. A conditionally disabled copy of the guard is still accepted, so the marquee fail-closed claim and its stated test-validity guarantee are not established.
